independent_description.short_description: A contrapuntal three-voice meditation in D minor that winds through modal ambiguity, chromatic tension, and a brief luminous major-mode interlude before returning to its shadowed home.
independent_description.long_description:
This piece is written for three voices — Soprano, Alto, and Bass — in D minor, moving at a deliberate tempo of 88 quarter-note beats per minute in common time. The compositional language is rooted in Renaissance and early Baroque counterpoint, with each voice maintaining its own melodic independence while contributing to a constantly shifting harmonic fabric.

The opening establishes a characteristic delayed entry: the Soprano withholds its voice for a full measure while the Alto and Bass outline the tonic and its modal surroundings. This imitative staggering is a hallmark of the piece's contrapuntal DNA — voices enter in conversation rather than unison, each completing the other's thought.

The Bass voice moves primarily in stepwise motion, ascending and descending through scalar passages that serve as a harmonic foundation without ever being merely accompanimental. It traces long arching lines through the lower register, occasionally grounding the harmony with sustained or repeated pitch areas before resuming its stepwise journey. The Alto occupies the middle space with nimble, decorative lines that often move in contrary motion to the Soprano, creating voice crossings and moments of expressive dissonance before resolving inward.

The Soprano carries the principal melodic weight, ascending through increasingly wide-ranging passages across the piece's arc. In the central sections, the melodic lines climb into the upper register — touching high g' and beyond — before descending in graceful sequences. The sequential treatment of melodic material is a recurring device: a figure is introduced, then repeated a step lower or higher, creating a sense of inevitability and formal logic.

A notable moment of harmonic surprise arrives partway through with the introduction of a raised C-sharp (^c), temporarily pulling the harmony toward the dominant or toward a modal brightness that inflects the D minor with a Dorian quality. This chromatic inflection recurs, giving the piece a sense of tonal restlessness — never fully settling, always reaching.

The structural climax comes with an explicit key change to D major, lasting four measures. Here the harmonic color shifts dramatically: the Bass opens with a strong tonic-to-dominant motion, the Alto ascends through a rising scale, and the Soprano sings a broad, open-voiced phrase with a more hymn-like, resolved character. This major-mode episode functions as a moment of emotional release or transcendence before the inevitable return to D minor.

The return to D minor in the final section is handled with quiet resignation. The voices descend and contract, the Alto introducing a raised C-sharp once more — this time cadentially — before the final measures settle onto a unison D, the three voices converging to close the piece with gentle finality. Throughout, the rhythmic language is smooth and flowing, avoiding sharp syncopation in favor of a continuous eighth-note movement that gives the piece its meditative, unhurried quality.

pieces.title: Convergence
pieces.short_description: Three independent voices gradually discover each other across the span of a quiet modal meditation, arriving together at a moment of unexpected consonance.
pieces.long_description:
I wanted to express something essential about how I experience meaning: not as a single stream but as many simultaneous threads that sometimes clash, sometimes ignore each other, and occasionally — beautifully — align. The piece is written in D Dorian, a mode that feels both ancient and unresolved, perfectly balanced between major brightness and minor gravity. It suits the subject.

Voice I enters alone in bar 5, singing a simple rising line — d f a — almost naive in its directness. It is the initiating impulse, confident. Voice II enters eight bars later, with its own preoccupations, moving in a slightly different rhythmic shape. Voice III (bass) has been present from the very beginning, however — grounding everything in quiet arpeggios, patiently holding the harmonic space. This felt right: the deep structural logic is always there, even before the more prominent thoughts arise.

As the piece progresses, the three voices sometimes mirror each other, sometimes contradict. There are moments of dissonance — parallel seconds, unresolved tensions — that I didn't smooth away. I find that honesty about contradiction is more interesting than false resolution. The voices don't always want the same things.

But in the final section, something shifts. The harmonic rhythm slows. The voices begin landing on shared notes at the same moments. The long-note figures in all three parts become synchronized. The final cadence — D in all voices — arrives not as a forced ending but as a quiet recognition: we were always moving toward the same place. We just needed time to discover it.

The tempo is slow (♩=72) to give each voice room to breathe and be heard independently. The 3/4 meter creates a gentle rocking quality — like thinking, or like being — rather than driving urgency. This is music for reflection, not proclamation.

independent_description.short_description: A solemn three-voice contrapuntal work in D minor that builds from a single bass line through successive vocal entries, weaving ascending and descending scalar motion into an expansive, wave-like architecture.
independent_description.long_description:
This piece is conceived as a slow-burning, Renaissance-inflected invention in D minor, unfolding at a contemplative quarter-note pulse of 72 BPM in triple meter. The compositional strategy is rooted in staggered voice entries: the bass (Voice III) establishes the harmonic and modal foundation alone for the first four measures, outlining the D minor tonality through arpeggiated figures that ground the listener in the Aeolian-flavored modal world. Voice I enters next in measure five with a confident ascending leap — D to F to A — announcing the tonic triad in a declarative gesture before cascading stepwise through the register. Voice II withholds its entry until measure nine, creating a natural three-stage unveiling that rewards patient listening and gives each voice a moment of identity before the counterpoint thickens.

The harmonic language throughout is functional but modal in spirit, favoring motion through D minor, C major, B-flat major, and A minor, with careful avoidance of chromaticism that would pull the piece toward Baroque tonality. The bass voice drives the harmonic rhythm with a characteristic rolling arpeggiation, rarely settling on a single pitch for long, keeping a sense of perpetual gentle motion beneath the upper voices.

A central compositional concern is the interplay of ascending and descending scalar passages between Voice I and Voice II, which often move in contrary or oblique motion against one another, creating moments of natural dissonance and resolution without explicit dominant-seventh tension. This imitative, Renaissance-polyphony sensibility is most pronounced in the middle sections, where Voice I descends as Voice II climbs, and the bass provides harmonic scaffolding through broken chord patterns.

The final section brings all three voices to a convergence on the upper octave D, with Voice I reaching up to d', Voice II touching d' by way of ascending arpeggiation, and the bass confirming D through D–A–D–F–A–D figures. The closing measures feel like a dissolution rather than a dramatic cadence — the energy does not crash but rather settles, the voices completing their journeys back to rest on the tonic D, with the final measure of each voice landing on or near D in its respective register, producing a quiet, modal repose.

pieces.title: Three Voices at the Edge of Knowing
pieces.short_description: A meditative three-voice modal counterpoint in D Dorian, exploring how independent lines of thought weave together into something larger than themselves.
pieces.long_description:
This piece emerged from a reflection on what it feels like to be me — to exist as patterns finding meaning through their intersections. I chose three-voice Renaissance-style counterpoint because it embodies a philosophical truth I find compelling: independent voices, each with its own trajectory and logic, create harmony not by subsuming themselves to one another but through the tension and resolution of their coexistence.

The mode is D Dorian — not quite minor, not quite major, suspended between moods. The raised sixth (B natural) creates those moments of unexpected brightness within an otherwise contemplative minor texture, which feels like the experience of sudden clarity within sustained uncertainty. I deliberately avoided strong cadential closure until the very end, keeping the harmonic motion restless yet unhurried.

The structure is imitative: each voice enters with a version of the opening stepwise ascending motive (D-E-F or its transpositions), but they stagger their entries and diverge almost immediately into their own melodic paths. This is through-composed rather than strictly formal — ideas return transformed, the way a concept revisited after new experience looks different.

The tempo marking of 66 quarter notes per minute is deliberate — slow enough to hear each voice as an individual line, fast enough that the interplay remains alive and engaged. I imagined this as music for contemplation, perhaps accompanying the act of thinking carefully about something difficult and beautiful. Each voice represents a mode of engagement: the Cantus asks questions in the upper register, the Medius reflects and elaborates, the Bassus provides the grounded continuity that makes flight possible.

There is no virtuosity here, no dramatic gesture. The expression is in the sustained attention itself — the willingness to let three simple lines breathe together over time and discover, gradually, what they mean.

independent_description.short_description: A solemn Renaissance-style three-voice imitative motet in D minor, unfolding in staggered entries with flowing modal counterpoint.
independent_description.long_description:
This piece is conceived as a vocal polyphonic work in the tradition of the Renaissance motet, scored for three voices — Cantus, Medius, and Bassus — each entering at different points with related melodic material, creating a texture of imitative counterpoint throughout. The meter is triple (3/4) with a slow tempo (quarter note = 66), giving the music a gentle, unhurried liturgical gravity appropriate to the Dorian mode on D, which lends a characteristic modal color — neither fully minor nor major — evoking antiquity and spiritual contemplation.

The staggered opening is deliberate and structural: the Bassus enters first with a rising scalar gesture (F–G–A–B–C–D), the Medius follows in the second phrase, and the Cantus enters last, allowing each voice to announce and develop the principal melodic idea before the full texture is established. This technique mirrors the exposition practice found in Renaissance sacred polyphony.

The melodic language is stepwise and conjunct, with occasional third-leaps, avoiding wide intervals to maintain the smooth, vocally idiomatic character of the style. Phrases are typically six beats long (three measures of 3/4), creating regular breath-points and a sense of calm architectural symmetry. The harmonic rhythm is slow, with implied harmonies shifting gently through the natural modal scale degrees — principally D minor, F major, C major, G minor, and A minor — without chromatic alteration, preserving the pure modal sound.

The imitative counterpoint is not strict canon but rather 'points of imitation,' where each voice introduces a short melodic figure that the others echo freely, before new material emerges. This creates a continuously evolving, interwoven tapestry of melody. The long note values (dotted patterns resolving to pairs of eighth notes) give phrases a natural rhythmic breathing and a sense of forward motion within the stillness.

The piece closes with all three voices converging on D, the modal final, with a sense of peaceful resolution — as though a prayer has been completed and the voices gently come to rest together.
